QuestionText: Health is defined by WHO as:
Options: B) A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: WHO definition of health: 'A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.'

Options: B) A condition where normal functioning is impaired
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Disease: a specific condition that impairs the normal functioning of an organism. Has specific causes (pathogens, deficiencies, genetics) and produces characteristic signs/symptoms.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Acute: rapid onset, short duration (common cold, cholera, typhoid). Chronic: long-lasting (tuberculosis, diabetes, cancer). Acute can be severe but resolves quickly.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Chronic diseases persist for a long time: diabetes (lifelong), tuberculosis (months), arthritis. Usually cause more damage to health than acute diseases over time.

Options: B) Pathogens (microorganisms) that can spread from person to person
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Infectious (communicable) diseases: caused by pathogens (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, worms). Can be transmitted (person to person, or via vector, water, air).

Options: B) Not caused by pathogens — cannot spread between persons
D) Less serious than infectious diseases
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Non-infectious: cancer, diabetes, heart disease, deficiency diseases (scurvy, rickets). Not caused by pathogens. Cannot be transmitted. Related to lifestyle, genetics, environment.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Antibiotics: substances that kill or inhibit bacteria. Have NO effect on viruses. Discovered by Fleming (penicillin). Specific antibiotics for specific bacteria.

Options: B) Stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies in advance
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Vaccines: introduce weakened/dead/fragments of pathogen. Immune system produces antibodies and memory cells. Future infection → rapid immune response → no disease.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome): caused by HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus). HIV attacks helper T-cells → weakens immune system → opportunistic infections.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Malaria: caused by Plasmodium (protozoan). Transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito. Infects RBCs → periodic fever. Treatment: antimalarials (quinine, chloroquine, artemisinin).

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: TB: caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Airborne transmission (coughing). Primarily affects lungs but can affect any organ. BCG vaccine provides protection.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Cholera: Vibrio cholerae, waterborne disease. Severe watery diarrhoea → dehydration. Transmitted through contaminated water and food. Prevented by clean water and sanitation.

QuestionText: The common cold is caused by:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Common cold: caused by rhinoviruses (200+ different viruses). Airborne and contact transmission. No effective vaccine (too many virus types). Antibiotics don't work.

Options: B) Intermediate organisms (vectors) like mosquitoes, ticks, fleas
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Vector-borne: an organism (vector) carries the pathogen and transmits to another host. Mosquito: malaria, dengue, filaria. Fly: typhoid. Flea: plague. Tick: Lyme disease.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Dengue: caused by dengue virus, transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquito (daytime biter). Symptoms: high fever, severe headache, joint pain ('breakbone fever'), rash.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Filariasis: caused by filarial worm Wuchereria bancrofti. Transmitted by Culex mosquito. Blocks lymph vessels → elephantiasis (swollen limbs, especially legs).

QuestionText: The immune system protects the body by:
Options: C) Producing antibodies and immune cells to fight pathogens
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Immune system: produces antibodies (proteins that bind and neutralise antigens), activates phagocytes (engulf pathogens), creates memory cells (rapid future response).

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Penicillin discovered by Alexander Fleming (1928) — he noticed mould (Penicillium) killed bacteria on his petri dish. First antibiotic. Revolutionised treatment of bacterial infections.

Options: B) Pathogens in food/drink by heating briefly to specific temperature
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Pasteurisation (Louis Pasteur): heat food/drink (e.g., milk) to 72°C for 15 seconds → kills pathogenic bacteria without significantly affecting taste. Used for milk, juice, wine.

QuestionText: Immunity acquired after recovering from a disease is:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Natural active immunity: body produces its own antibodies after exposure to pathogen during natural infection. Long-lasting. Vaccination = artificial active immunity.

Options: B) Sustained high fever, headache, abdominal pain
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Typhoid: caused by Salmonella typhi (bacterium). Waterborne. Symptoms: sustained high fever (39-40°C), headache, weakness, abdominal pain. Widal test diagnoses it.

QuestionText: The Widal test is used to diagnose:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Widal test: detects antibodies against Salmonella typhi in blood. Used to diagnose typhoid fever. Positive after 2nd week of infection.

QuestionText: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Scurvy: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency. Symptoms: bleeding gums, poor wound healing, joint pain. Vitamin C essential for collagen synthesis.

QuestionText: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Rickets: Vitamin D deficiency in children → impaired calcium absorption → weak, soft, deformed bones. Adults: osteomalacia. Sunlight exposure + dietary sources.

QuestionText: The causative agent of plague is:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Plague: Yersinia pestis. Transmitted by rat fleas. Three forms: bubonic (lymph nodes), pneumonic (lungs), septicaemic (blood). Historical Black Death killed 1/3 of Europe.

QuestionText: Antiseptics and disinfectants prevent disease by:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Antiseptics: applied to living tissue (wounds, skin) to prevent infection. Disinfectants: applied to non-living surfaces. Examples: Dettol, iodine, alcohol, bleach (for surfaces).

Options: C) Bite of infected animal (dog, bat)
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Rabies: caused by lyssavirus. Transmitted through saliva of infected animals (bite/scratch). Attacks nervous system → invariably fatal once symptoms appear. Vaccine available (post-exposure).

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Hepatitis B: HBV (Hepatitis B Virus). Attacks liver. Transmitted: blood, sexual contact, mother to child. Can cause chronic liver disease and cancer. Vaccine available.

QuestionText: Prevention is better than cure because:
Options: B) Prevention is cheaper, avoids suffering, and prevents disease spread
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Prevention: cheaper, avoids suffering, stops spread. Methods: vaccination, hygiene, sanitation, safe food/water, vector control, proper nutrition.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Polio: poliovirus infects motor neurons → muscle paralysis. Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) = Sabin vaccine. Injectable (IPV) = Salk vaccine. India certified polio-free in 2014.

Options: B) Some bacteria survive antibiotic treatment and multiply
C) Patients take too many antibiotics
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Antibiotic resistance: natural selection. Bacteria with random mutations survive antibiotic → multiply → resistant population. Accelerated by incomplete antibiotic courses, overuse.

QuestionText: Jaundice (yellow skin/eyes) is a symptom of:
Options: B) Liver disease (hepatitis, obstruction of bile duct)
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Jaundice: yellowish tinge due to excess bilirubin (from RBC breakdown) in blood. Liver normally processes bilirubin. Liver damage/hepatitis → bilirubin accumulates.

QuestionText: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Night blindness (nyctalopia): Vitamin A deficiency. Vitamin A needed to produce rhodopsin (visual pigment in rod cells). Also causes xerophthalmia (dry eyes), corneal damage.

QuestionText: BCG vaccine is given to prevent:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guerin): vaccine against tuberculosis. Given at birth. Provides significant protection against severe forms of TB in children.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Waterborne diseases prevented by safe water: typhoid, cholera, dysentery (bacterial), hepatitis A (viral), giardiasis (protozoan). Boiling, chlorination, filtration ensure safety.

Options: B) Improper nutrition — overnutrition OR undernutrition OR specific deficiencies
C) Eating too many calories only
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Malnutrition: inadequate nutrition. Includes undernutrition (too little food/nutrients), overnutrition (obesity), or specific deficiencies (vitamin A, iron, iodine, etc.).

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Iodine deficiency: thyroid can't produce thyroxine → thyroid enlarges (goitre). In pregnancy: cretinism in foetus. Iodised salt prevents it.

Options: C) Leishmania donovani (protozoan), transmitted by sandfly
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis): caused by Leishmania donovani (protozoan). Transmitted by female Phlebotomus sandfly. Affects liver, spleen, bone marrow. Endemic in Bihar/Jharkhand.

QuestionText: The first vaccine was developed by Edward Jenner against:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Edward Jenner (1796): vaccinated boy with cowpox → protected against smallpox. First vaccine. 'Vaccine' from Latin 'vacca' = cow. Smallpox eradicated globally in 1980.

QuestionText: Signs of disease are different from symptoms because:
Options: A) They are the same thing
B) Signs are objectively measured (by doctor); symptoms are subjectively felt by patient
C) Symptoms are measured by doctor
D) Signs are only seen in chronic disease
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Symptoms: what patient experiences (fever, pain, fatigue). Signs: objective, measurable evidence (elevated temperature on thermometer, rash visible, abnormal blood test).

QuestionText: Communicable diseases spread from person to person by:
Options: A) Direct contact, droplets, vectors, contaminated food/water
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Communicable disease spread: direct contact (skin diseases), airborne droplets (TB, cold, flu), vectors (mosquito, fly), contaminated food/water (cholera, typhoid).

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Antivirals: drugs targeting viral infections. E.g., oseltamivir (Tamiflu) for influenza, acyclovir for herpes, antiretrovirals (ARVs) for HIV/AIDS. Fewer than antibiotics — viruses are harder to target.

QuestionText: Sleeping sickness (African trypanosomiasis) is caused by:
Options: C) Trypanosoma (protozoan), transmitted by tsetse fly
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Sleeping sickness: Trypanosoma brucei (protozoan). Transmitted by tsetse fly. Attacks nervous system → disrupts sleep-wake cycle. Fatal if untreated. Endemic in sub-Saharan Africa.

QuestionText: The most important personal hygiene practice preventing disease spread is:
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Handwashing: single most effective personal hygiene measure. Removes pathogens from hands. Prevents faecal-oral diseases (cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A, diarrhoea).

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Diabetes: non-infectious hormonal disease. Type 1: autoimmune, insufficient insulin. Type 2: insulin resistance. Not caused by pathogen, cannot spread between persons.

Options: B) Clean water, proper sanitation, healthcare access, pollution control
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Community health: requires clean water supply, proper waste disposal, sewage treatment, vaccination programs, healthcare access, education about hygiene — not just individual behaviour.

QuestionText: The function of WBCs (leucocytes) in disease is:
Options: B) Defend against pathogens (phagocytosis, antibody production)
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: WBCs (white blood cells): immune defence. Neutrophils: phagocytose bacteria. Lymphocytes: produce antibodies (B-cells), attack cells (T-cells). Monocytes: phagocytose large particles.

Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Dengue: virus affects platelet-producing cells → platelet count drops. Dangerously low platelets → bleeding risk. NS1 antigen test or ELISA diagnoses dengue.

QuestionText: Proper food storage prevents disease by:
Options: B) Preventing microbial growth and toxin production
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Refrigeration: slows bacterial growth. Boiling: kills pathogens. Canning: creates anaerobic environment. Prevents food poisoning (Salmonella, Staphylococcus aureus, Clostridium botulinum).

QuestionText: Which disease was declared eradicated worldwide by WHO in 1980?
Topic: Biology - Why Do We Fall Ill
Explanation: Smallpox: declared eradicated in 1980 by WHO — the only human infectious disease to be fully eradicated through a global vaccination programme. Last natural case: 1977.
